## Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| echo: false
data <- read.csv("./template_workshop_feedback_form.csv", header = TRUE)
data <- data[data$ended != "",]
registration <- 25
LMUregistration <- 20
Attendees <- 23
```

We received `r registration` registrations (`r round(LMUregistration/registration*100,0)` % of which LMU members). `r Attendees` attended (`r round(Attendees/registration*100,0)` % of registrants).

Total number of respondents in this feedback survey: **`r nrow(data)`** (`r round(nrow(data)/Attendees*100)`% of attendees)

## Session rating

The session was rated from 0 ('I do not recommend it') to 5 ('I fully recommend it'). On average, the session was rated `r round(mean(data$ratinga, na.rm=TRUE),2)` (min = `r min(data$ratinga, na.rm=TRUE)`, max = `r max(data$ratinga, na.rm=TRUE)`, **median =** **`r median(data$ratinga, na.rm= TRUE)`**).

## Pre and post confidence in ability

We asked their level of confidence in their ability to adopt the skill XX before and after the workshop.

```{r}
#| echo: false

  # Convert "na" strings to NA if needed
  data$prior[data$prior == "na"] <- NA
  data$post[data$post == "na"]   <- NA
  
  # Reshape to long format
  data_long <- data %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(prior, post),
                 names_to = "time",
                 values_to = "confidence") %>%
    mutate(
      time = factor(recode(time, prior = "Before", post = "After"),
                    levels = c("Before", "After")),
      confidence = as.numeric(confidence),
      confidence_jittered = confidence + runif(n(), -0.1, 0.1)
    )
  
  # Plot
  ggplot(data_long, aes(x = time, y = confidence_jittered, group = iteration)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.4, color = "gray60", na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "gray40", na.rm = TRUE) +
    stat_summary(aes(y = confidence, group = 1),
                 fun = mean, geom = "line", color = "blue", linewidth = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    stat_summary(aes(y = confidence, group = 1),
                 fun = mean, geom = "point", color = "blue", size = 3, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = 0:3,
      labels = c("Not confident at all",
                 "Mostly not confident",
                 "Somewhat confident",
                 "Very confident"),
      limits = c(0, 3)
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "",
      y = "",
      title = paste("Confidence in XX")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5) # 
    )


```

## Suitability of the workshops format for the content to be delivered

We asked: "Do you think the training methods applied in the workshop, e.g. workshop format or exercises, were appropriate for the respective workshop content?".

```{r}
#| echo: false

N <- c(
table(data$appropriate)['0'],
table(data$appropriate)['1'],
table(data$appropriate)['2'],
table(data$appropriate)['3'],
table(data$appropriate)['na'])

N[is.na(N)] <- 0

Answer <- c("Not appropriate at all",
"Somewhat inappropriate",
"Somewhat appropriate",
"Very appropriate",
"Unsure/not applicable")

summary_appropriate <- cbind(Answer, N
                          )

colnames(summary_appropriate)[1] <- "Were the training method appropriate for the workshop content?"
rownames(summary_appropriate) <- NULL
knitr::kable(summary_appropriate)

```

Comments associated to this question were:

```{r echo = FALSE}
data$inappropriate[data$inappropriate != '']

```

## Level of the workshop

```{r}
#| echo = FALSE

levels <- data[,startsWith(colnames(data), "level")]

levels[levels == ''] <- NA
levels[levels == 'muchdifficult'] <- 1
levels[levels == 'difficult'] <- 2
levels[levels == 'right'] <- 3
levels[levels == 'easy'] <- 4
levels[levels == 'mucheasy'] <- 5

prior <- data[,startsWith(colnames(data), "prior")]
prior[prior == 'na'] <- NA

prior_levels_long <- data.frame(cbind(levels = unlist(levels), prior = unlist(prior)))
prior_levels_wide <- cbind(levels, prior)
```

The workshop was targeted at novices in XX. It welcomed early career researchers from various disciplines and diverse prior knowledge.

Overall, we expect participants with increasing prior knowledge to find our training material increasingly easy as it is primarily targeted at novices.

```{r}
#| echo = FALSE
par(mar=c(4,10,1,1)+.1)
sunflowerplot (prior_levels_long$levels ~ prior_levels_long$prior, ylim = c(1,5), xlim = c(0,3), xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n" ,  xlab = "Prior knowledge" , ylab ="")
axis(1, at = 0:3, labels = c('none', 'basic', 'advanced', 'expert'))
axis(2, at = 1:5, labels = c('much too difficult', 'slightly too difficult', 'about right', 'slightly too easy','much too easy'),las=1 )      
title(ylab = "Level of the workshop", line = 9)   

```
